subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.2 'FUNCTION</u> <u>YEAR-TO-YYYY' OK (General format) - the format is 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )', both words underlined hence required, with argument-3 NESTED inside argument-2's brackets. READ: there is no bespoke grammar for this function - CobolExpressions.g4's functionCall carries 'FUNCTION functionName' plus a parenthesised argument list of arithmeticExpressions separated by §8.3.5 separators, and IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 205 supplies the shape: Add(new("YEAR-TO-YYYY", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, 1, 3, "iii", "YearToYyyy", ...)). IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore line 573 enforces it - 'if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)' => COBOL1504 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY takes 1..3 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. The BRACKET NESTING needs no separate rule: the arguments are positional, so 1, 2 or 3 written arguments is exactly the language the nested brackets generate (argument-3 cannot be written without argument-2). Result type Integer matches §15.100.1 'The type of the function is integer'. Every arity is live in code - the 3-argument form is pinned end to end by conformance:cases/15.23.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_date_window (11 hand-derived lines), the 1-argument form by unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear; only the 2-argument form has no test, and no fixture pins the COBOL1504 over- or under-arity rejection for this function. The below-2002 edition gate is pinned by conformance:cases/_unassigned/date_window_below_2002 (COBOL1502). NOTE for the reader of AR-15.100.3-5: the 1- and 2-argument forms PARSE and COMPILE correctly on every carrier - the divergence recorded there is in the runtime default, not in this format. REFUTED: REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS - the implementation reading survives independent re-derivation - but ONE EVIDENCE CLAIM IS FALSE AND IS WITHDRAWN. cite.py --check 15.100.2 'YEAR-TO-YYYY' -> OK §15.100.2 (General format), rendering '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>YEAR-TO-YYYY</u> ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )'. I verified every arity edge by READING, not by sampling: IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 205 gives IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing with MinArgs 1 / MaxArgs 3; IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore computes 'long given = args.Sum(...)' and rejects 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' with COBOL1504 before any per-function arm; and I confirmed the binder injects NO default argument for this function (the only injecting arm is BindNumvalCFamily), so the written arity survives to the renderer intact - which is precisely what makes the bracket nesting positional and correct. THE FALSE CLAIM: 'the 1-argument form [is pinned] by unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear'. It is not. That test (CobolDateWindowingTests.cs line 41) calls 'CobolDate.YearToYyyy(76)' - a direct C# call on the runtime API. It never compiles a COBOL one-argument reference and so exercises none of the grammar, the catalog arity, the binder's COBOL1504, or the renderer's arity-dependent emission. The one-argument SOURCE form has no test on any path, and per the REFUTED note on AR-15.100.3-3 it is in fact the broken form on the float carrier. The two-argument source form is likewise untested, and no negative fixture pins the COBOL1504 over- or under-arity rejection for this function. That is a test debt, not an implementation gap - rule 3 makes CONFORMS with a thin test-ref a legitimate outcome - so the verdict stands and the claim is struck. EDITIONS (rule 4): '2002,2014,2023' is NOT taken from IntrinsicCatalog's own 2002 field nor from ConstructRegistry.g.cs, both of which are the code under review. Annex E of the 2023 standard carries no §15.100 entry (it lists changes from 2014), and the value matches the landed sibling inventory rows FMT-15.23.2 / FMT-15.25.2 for the same Y2K trio.
